rituals.title: MAKE THE BELIEF BET
rituals.goal: Let one behaviour test what argument cannot settle.
rituals.steps:
1. State Belief — State the belief as a clear prediction.
2. Choose Safe — Choose a safe, small action that could prove it wrong as well as right.
3. Picture Outcome — Hold the expected result before acting.
4. Test Observation — Run the test, then compare observation with prediction.
5. Pay Out — Pay out only to evidence.
rituals.win: ✓ Evidence won the bet. Belief did not get a sympathy payout.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Pay Out”; release the score.
• Pulled back? Touch “Picture Outcome”.
• “Test Observation” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• “State Belief” versus “Pay Out”: what eased?
• I can use “Choose Safe” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: State Belief → Choose Safe → Picture Outcome → Test Observation → Pay Out
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Cancel any experiment involving danger, coercion, medical risk, or another person’s consent.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE EFFORT STAIRCASE
rituals.goal: Start where movement is possible, not where pride prefers.
rituals.steps:
1. Name — Name five versions of the task from almost easy to really stretching.
2. Cross Out — Remove the zero-effort decoy.
3. Remain Version — Do the smallest remaining version that leaves visible evidence—one paragraph, one call, one plate washed.
4. Climb Stair — Next time, climb only one stair.
rituals.win: ✓ One stair was enough to create movement.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Climb Stair”; release the score.
• On return, repeat “Remain Version”.
• “Remain Version” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• What lost power: “Name” → “Climb Stair”?
• I can use “Cross Out” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: Name → Cross Out → Remain Version → Climb Stair
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Reduce the step further if illness, exhaustion, or overload is being ignored.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: TWO ENGINES
rituals.goal: Pleasure and mastery refuel different parts of you.
rituals.steps:
1. Schedule Chosen — For the next day, schedule one act chosen purely for enjoyment and one chosen for competence.
2. Make Small — Make both small enough to happen.
3. Check Both — After each activity, ask which engine it fed: pleasure or mastery. Rate that one channel only.
4. Drop Demand — Do not demand that either activity fix everything.
rituals.win: ✓ Good-enough became usable again.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Drop Demand”; release the score.
• If it flares, choose “Check Both”.
• “Check Both” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• “Drop Demand”: what changed from “Schedule Chosen”?
• I can use “Make Small” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: Schedule Chosen → Make Small → Check Both → Drop Demand

Pleasure and mastery refuel different parts of you.

RITUAL
1. Schedule Chosen — For the next day, schedule one act chosen purely for enjoyment and one chosen for competence.
2. Make Small — Make both small enough to happen.
3. Check Both — After each activity, ask which engine it fed: pleasure or mastery. Rate that one channel only.
4. Drop Demand — Do not demand that either activity fix everything.

WIN
✓ Good-enough became usable again.

• Exhale after “Drop Demand”; release the score.
• If it flares, choose “Check Both”.
• “Check Both” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• “Drop Demand”: what changed from “Schedule Chosen”?
• I can use “Make Small” without perfecting.

FORMULA FLOW
Schedule Chosen → Make Small → Check Both → Drop Demand

PAUSE
Rebalance if achievement becomes punishment or pleasure becomes avoidance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: MAKE THE ROOM VOTE
rituals.goal: Your environment casts ballots before willpower arrives.
rituals.steps:
1. Pick Desired — Pick one desired behaviour and one unwanted default.
2. Place Object — Place the first object needed for the desired action directly in your path.
3. Add Deliberate — Add one small obstacle to the unwanted route: distance, logout, container, timer, or removal.
4. Let Space Vote — Let the room make the better vote easier.
rituals.win: ✓ The room tipped the vote toward the choice I actually want.

• Re-entry move: “Add Deliberate”.
• “Add Deliberate” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• “Pick Desired” to “Let Space Vote”: what loosened?
• I can use “Place Object” without perfecting.

rituals.title: LET THE URGE MISS ITS APPOINTMENT
rituals.goal: The ritual expects you; do not show up.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Cue — Name the cue and the usual calming act it normally summons.
2. Contact — Contact only a manageable dose of the cue.
3. Keep Hands — Keep your hands and attention out of the ritual while the urge changes on its own.
4. Mark Peak — Hold the peak and the first natural drop.
5. Let Learning Land — The learning comes from not doing the old ritual.
rituals.win: ✓ The urge stayed loud without taking the wheel.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Let Learning Land”; let wanting crest.
• Skip replay; use “Keep Hands”.
• “Mark Peak” keeps wanting off controls.
• Compare “Name Cue” with “Let Learning Land”.
• I can use “Contact” without obeying the urge.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Cue → Contact → Keep Hands → Mark Peak → Let Learning Land

rituals.title: WHEN/THEN FIRMWARE
rituals.goal: Pre-decide the moment that usually steals the decision.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Line — Picture one line only: WHEN [specific visible cue], THEN I WILL [small physical action].
2. Remove Vague — Remove vague words such as try, soon, or better.
3. Imagine Cue — Imagine the cue once, do the action once, and place the rule where the cue occurs.
4. Skip Pep Talk — Skip the pep talk.

• Skip replay; use “Imagine Cue”.

• “Picture Line” to “Skip Pep Talk”: what loosened?
• I can use “Remove Vague” without rushing.

rituals.title: RIDE THE CRAVING GRAPH
rituals.goal: An urge is a curve pretending to be a command.
rituals.steps:
1. Level — Notice its current level and where it moves in the body.
2. Watch Slope — Watch for slope: rising, flattening, cresting, falling.
3. Imagine Urge — Every thirty seconds, imagine the next point without acting on the urge.
4. Name Change — When the line changes direction, name the change.
5. Choose Time — Choose what protects the next hour.
rituals.win: ✓ The craving curved; the next hour kept the vote.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Time”; let wanting crest.
• Re-entry move: “Imagine Urge”.
• “Name Change” keeps wanting off controls.
• What lost power: “Level” → “Choose Time”?
• I can use “Watch Slope” without obeying the urge.
rituals.formula_flow: Level → Watch Slope → Imagine Urge → Name Change → Choose Time
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.title: OBJECTIVE OVER EGO
rituals.goal: The best move may not be the most satisfying proof.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Real — Picture the real objective in seven words or fewer.
2. Name — Name the action that advances it and the action that merely wins, punishes, impresses, or avoids embarrassment.
3. Imagine Tomorrow — Imagine tomorrow’s result after each.
4. Select Works — Select what works, even if the ego receives no trophy.
rituals.win: ✓ The picture widened beyond the selected facts.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Select Works”; slow the clock.
• Re-entry move: “Imagine Tomorrow”.
• “Imagine Tomorrow” puts facts above speed.
• “Picture Real” versus “Select Works”: what eased?
• I can use “Name” without rushing.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture Real → Name → Imagine Tomorrow → Select Works
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Revisit the objective if it excludes dignity, consent, or safety.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.steps:
1. Use Cool — Use cool—not painfully cold—water or a wrapped cool pack on the cheeks and around the eyes for a brief interval.

rituals.title: BURN THE EXCESS CHARGE
rituals.goal: Give body alarm a finish line.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Burst — Choose a contained burst: fast stairs, wall pushes, brisk marching, or another safe vigorous movement.
2. Set Short — Set a short timer before starting.
3. End Completely — When it ends, stop completely, feel the after-pulse, and drink water.
4. Let Body — Let the body spend energy without spending your future.
rituals.win: ✓ Panic became a wave with surroundings around it.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Let Body”; no breath-holding.
• Restart detected: “End Completely”.

• “Choose Burst” → “Let Body”: what changed?
• I can use “Set Short” while alarm rises.

rituals.goal: Make urgency leave through a gentler exit.
rituals.steps:

4. Breathe Workable — After several rounds, resume natural breathing and look for one workable decision.

rituals.title: STAY FOR THE UPDATE
rituals.goal: Safe contact gives fear new data.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose External — Choose an external cue low enough on your fear ladder to approach voluntarily.
2. Enter Escape — Enter without escape and remain until you observe at least one mismatch between prediction and reality.
3. Name Mismatch — Name the mismatch before leaving.
4. Repeat Later — Repeat later under safe conditions rather than chasing maximum distress.
rituals.win: ✓ The future reopened beyond the alarm.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Repeat Later”; leave the forecast.
• Restart detected: “Name Mismatch”.
• “Name Mismatch” — fear isn’t fate.
• “Repeat Later”: what changed from “Choose External”?
• I can use “Enter Escape” while fear stays loud.

rituals.title: THE CONTROLLED REPLAY
rituals.goal: A feared scene needs a container, not a flood.
rituals.steps:
1. Set Time — Set a start time, endpoint, grounding object, and recovery plan.
2. Recount — Recount or visualise the feared scene at a manageable pace without changing key facts.
3. Prediction — Notice shifts in prediction or emotion across the telling.
4. Finish Location — Finish by naming present location and date.

rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Finish Location”; notice the room.
• Catch restart with “Prediction”.
• “Prediction” proves the present returned.
• Before/after: “Set Time” → “Finish Location”.
• I can use “Recount” to return here.

rituals.title: LEAVE ONE QUESTION OPEN
rituals.goal: Uncertainty can remain unfinished without becoming an emergency.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Low — Choose a low-stakes unknown.
2. Picture Card — Picture it on a card and forbid checking, asking, or mentally solving until a set time.
3. Carry Unanswered — Carry the unanswered card while doing normal life.
4. Watch The Urge — At review, notice what the urge did—not whether certainty arrived.
rituals.win: ✓ The unanswered part stopped demanding immediate closure.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Watch The Urge”; leave it unanswered.
• Use “Carry Unanswered” on return.
• “Carry Unanswered” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• “Choose Low” → “Watch The Urge”: what changed?
• I can use “Picture Card” without a guarantee.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Low → Picture Card → Carry Unanswered → Watch The Urge

rituals.title: STAY THROUGH RECOVERY
rituals.goal: Stay long enough to learn what happens after the peak.
rituals.steps:
1. Highest — During a safe practice round, notice the highest point and the first downward shift.
2. Stay Past Relief — Do not leave at that first relief.
3. Remain Cue — Remain with the cue through a visible recovery phase—steady gaze, slower movement, reduced urge—then end on purpose.
4. Leave After Recovery — Departure follows learning, not panic.
rituals.win: ✓ Exit came after recovery—not at panic’s command.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Leave After Recovery”; no breath-holding.
• On return: “Remain Cue”.
• “Remain Cue” — alarm isn’t command.
• “Highest” → “Leave After Recovery”: what changed?
• I can use “Stay Past Relief” while alarm rises.
rituals.formula_flow: Highest → Stay Past Relief → Remain Cue → Leave After Recovery

rituals.title: REMOVE ONE INVISIBLE CRUTCH
rituals.goal: A crutch can hide the safety already holding you.
rituals.steps:
1. Identify Protective — During a manageable practice round, spot one protective act that is unnecessary: gripping, rehearsing, sitting by the exit, checking pulse, carrying extra certainty.
2. Drop Legitimate — Drop only that act while keeping legitimate safety intact.
3. Observe Outcome — Observe what the outcome says without it.
rituals.win: ✓ Pressure separated from importance.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Observe Outcome”; slow the clock.
• Pulled back? Touch “Drop Legitimate”.
• “Drop Legitimate” puts facts above speed.
• What lost power: “Identify Protective” → “Observe Outcome”?
• I can use “Drop Legitimate” without rushing.
rituals.formula_flow: Identify Protective → Drop Legitimate → Observe Outcome

rituals.title: MOVE THE LESSON
rituals.goal: Learning that works in one room may not travel by itself.
rituals.steps:
1. Repeat Mastered — Repeat a mastered practice while changing one feature: location, time, cue order, duration, or intensity.
2. Change Again — On the next round, alter a different feature.
3. Map Transfer — Keep a small mental map of where the skill still works.
4. Make Portable — Let variation turn a local success into portable knowledge.
rituals.win: ✓ The lesson travelled. It no longer belongs to one room.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Make Portable”; keep both sides.
• Use “Map Transfer” on return.
• “Map Transfer” widens the evidence field.
• At “Make Portable”, compare “Repeat Mastered”.
• I can use “Change Again” before concluding.
rituals.formula_flow: Repeat Mastered → Round → Keep Small → Turn Local

rituals.title: THE TWO-CUE MERGE
rituals.goal: Combine mastered signals only after each can stand alone.
rituals.steps:
1. Select Triggers — Select two triggers already manageable separately.
2. Predict Joining — Predict what joining them will add.
3. Drop Unnecessary — Contact both at a modest dose while dropping unnecessary escape.
4. Stay Long — Stay long enough to compare the combined result with the prediction, then recover fully.
rituals.win: ✓ Fear kept a warning, not a prophecy.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Stay Long”; leave the forecast.
• On return: “Drop Unnecessary”.
• “Drop Unnecessary” — fear isn’t fate.
• “Select Triggers” → “Stay Long”: what changed?
• I can use “Predict Joining” while fear stays loud.

rituals.title: TURN UP THE WHISPER
rituals.goal: A tiny movement may be the body’s unfinished instruction.
rituals.steps:
1. Smallest — Notice the smallest spontaneous tendency: sway, curl, stretch, turn, reach.
2. Pause Enlarge — Enlarge it by only ten percent and pause.
3. Ask Whether — Check if it brings ease, protection, energy, or nothing.
4. Let Determine — Let the answer determine whether to continue, reverse, or stop.
rituals.win: ✓ The whisper became clear enough to guide the next choice.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Let Determine”; no forcing.
• Shortcut: “Ask Whether”, once.
• “Ask Whether” keeps sensation as data.
• “Smallest” → “Let Determine”: what changed?
• I can use “Pause Enlarge” while sensation stays.
rituals.formula_flow: Smallest → Pause Enlarge → Ask Whether → Let Determine

rituals.goal: Give the body proof that time has moved.

rituals.title: FEAR WITHOUT THE MOVIE
rituals.goal: At the peak, meet energy before narrative claims it.
rituals.steps:
1. Locate Most — If safely steady, locate the most intense fear sensation and say only its movement, charge, heat, and boundary.
2. Remove Prediction — Remove prediction briefly.
3. Keep Hand — Keep one hand or gaze anchored in the room.
4. Let Raw — Let raw body alarm be observed without following its film script.
rituals.win: ✓ Fear became body energy before it could become a movie.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Let Raw”; then keep moving.
• Restart detected: “Keep Hand”.
• “Keep Hand” proves motion is available.
• “Locate Most” → “Let Raw”: what changed?
• I can use “Remove Prediction” before motivation.
rituals.formula_flow: Locate Most → Remove Prediction → Keep Hand → Let Raw
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.title: STUDY THE REACTION, NOT THE CHARACTER
rituals.goal: Self-inquiry works better as disciplined research.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Recurring — Choose a reaction that happens often and remember three times it happened.
2. Read Pattern — For each time, notice the trigger, meaning, body feeling, action, and result.
3. Compare Trusted — Compare the three examples with a trusted idea or guide.
4. Test One Guess — Choose one idea to test. Leave your whole character out of the experiment.
rituals.win: ✓ One reaction became a testable clue, not a character verdict.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Test One Guess”; no forcing.
• Use “Compare Trusted” on return.
• “Compare Trusted” keeps sensation as data.
• At “Test One Guess”, compare “Choose Recurring”.
• I can use “Read Pattern” while sensation stays.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Recurring → Read Pattern → Compare Trusted → Test One Guess

rituals.title: WHAT REMAINS WHEN REWARD LEAVES?
rituals.goal: Duty becomes clearer after fear and praise exit the room.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Role — Name your role, the people affected, and the values governing it.
2. Remove Applause — Mentally remove applause, punishment, and personal advantage.
3. Ask Responsibility — Ask which responsibility still stands.
4. Set Role Limit — Convert that answer into a time-bound action and one limit on what the role does not require.
rituals.win: ✓ The reward disappeared; the part I still cared about stayed.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Set Role Limit”; keep the compass.
• If it flares, choose “Ask Responsibility”.
• “Ask Responsibility” keeps meaning in motion.
• At “Set Role Limit”, compare “Name Role”.
• I can use “Remove Applause” while pain stays real.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Role → Remove Applause → Ask Responsibility → Set Role Limit

rituals.goal: A larger recipient can change the flavour of effort.
rituals.steps:
1. Select Behaviour — Select a behaviour; spot who or what it serves beyond immediate reward: a child, patient, craft, community, future generation, or principle.

3. Keep Quality — Keep quality high even if nobody knows.

• I can use “Act Offering” while sensation stays.

rituals.title: THE FIVE-BRICK REPAIR
rituals.goal: Reconnection is built from specific materials.
rituals.steps:
1. Build Repair — Build five bricks in order: the event without spin; the impact without defence; your responsibility without dilution; the unmet need; one concrete repair action.
2. Ask Evidence — Decide what changed behaviour would look like over time.
3. Make It Real — Treat the apology as the doorway and the changed behaviour as the proof.
rituals.win: ✓ I rebuilt repair from five bricks, not from one polished apology.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Make It Real”; release extra blame.
• Re-entry move: “Ask Evidence”.
• “Ask Evidence” keeps blame in proportion.
• “Make It Real”: what changed from “Build Repair”?
• I can use “Ask Evidence” without owning everything.
rituals.formula_flow: Build Repair → Ask Evidence → Apology

rituals.title: MOVE THE CHARGE INTO A CONTAINER
rituals.goal: Body alarm needs a route with walls.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Shaking — Choose shaking, pushing a wall, stamping, stretching, or strong walking.
2. Start Define — Define space, duration, and maximum intensity before starting.
3. Keep Movement — Keep movement nonviolent and stop at the timer.
4. Take Earliest Move — Stand still afterward until you notice the earliest settling marker.
rituals.win: ✓ Gave the charge a container and stayed long enough to feel it settle.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Take Earliest Move”; then keep moving.
• Return once to “Keep Movement”.
• “Keep Movement” proves motion is available.
• “Choose Shaking” versus “Take Earliest Move”: what eased?
• I can use “Start Define” before motivation.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Shaking → Start Define → Keep Movement → Take Earliest Move

rituals.title: ANGER WITH WALLS
rituals.goal: Power may be expressed without becoming a weapon.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Private — Choose a private space and a short timer.
2. State Anger — State the anger plainly. Then imagine pushing the charge into a wall, or press your palms together firmly for a few seconds—without rehearsing violence.
3. Open Hands — When time ends, open hands, name the boundary underneath, and select a safe action.
rituals.win: ✓ Anger kept its power and lost its weapon.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Open Hands”; release extra load.
• Skip replay; use “State Anger”.
• “State Anger” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• Look back: “Choose Private” → “Open Hands”.
• I can use “State Anger” without carrying it all.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Private → State Anger → Open Hands
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Leave immediately and get help if there is risk of harming anyone or damaging property.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

RITUAL
1. Choose Private — Choose a private space and a short timer.
2. State Anger — State the anger plainly. Then imagine pushing the charge into a wall, or press your palms together firmly for a few seconds—without rehearsing violence.
3. Open Hands — When time ends, open hands, name the boundary underneath, and select a safe action.

WIN
✓ Anger kept its power and lost its weapon.

• Exhale after “Open Hands”; release extra load.
• Skip replay; use “State Anger”.
• “State Anger” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• Look back: “Choose Private” → “Open Hands”.
• I can use “State Anger” without carrying it all.

FORMULA FLOW
Choose Private → State Anger → Open Hands

PAUSE
Leave immediately and get help if there is risk of harming anyone or damaging property.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: BREAK THE DEADLINE MONOLITH
rituals.goal: Time pressure shrinks when it gains windows.
rituals.steps:
1. Count Usable — Count the usable work blocks remaining, subtracting sleep and fixed duties.
2. Give Block — Give each block one deliverable with a visible finish.
3. Place Buffers — Place buffers before the final deadline.
4. Start Earliest — Start the earliest window; refuse to mentally carry later windows inside it.
rituals.win: ✓ The decision regained enough space to be a decision.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Start Earliest”; slow the clock.
• Shortcut: “Place Buffers”, once.
• “Place Buffers” puts facts above speed.
• Before/after: “Count Usable” → “Start Earliest”.
• I can use “Give Block” without rushing.

rituals.title: TWENTY SECONDS BEFORE THE STORY
rituals.goal: Let sensation stay fluid before language freezes it.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Causes — For twenty seconds, ban emotion names and causes.
2. Describe Geometry — Say only geometry and physics: shape, temperature, pressure, texture, direction, pulse.
3. Choose Smallest — At the bell, choose the smallest Name that fits, or keep it unnamed if none does.
rituals.win: ✓ Sensation stayed fluid long enough to avoid becoming a premature story.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Smallest”; let feeling settle.
• Use “Describe Geometry” on return.
• “Describe Geometry” separates feeling from fact.
• “Name Causes” to “Choose Smallest”: what loosened?
• I can use “Describe Geometry” while emotion stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Causes → Describe Geometry → Choose Smallest
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop internal focus if it triggers panic, feeling unreal or disconnected, or pain concern.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: NO-CONCEPT MINUTE
rituals.goal: Reality gets one minute without explanation.
rituals.steps:
1. Set Brief — Set a brief interval.
2. Name Comparisons — During it, do not create causes, labels, comparisons, or solutions.
3. Attend Direct — Attend to direct colour, sound, contact, and movement.
4. Let Sensory — If a concept appears, acknowledge ‘explanation’ and let the sensory world continue.
rituals.win: ✓ For one minute, reality did not need my commentary.
rituals.supports:

• Catch restart with “Attend Direct”.
• “Attend Direct” proves the present returned.
• “Set Brief” to “Let Sensory”: what loosened?
• I can use “Name Comparisons” to return here.

rituals.title: MUTE THE INNER SUBTITLES
rituals.goal: One ordinary event requires no running review.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Washing — Choose washing, walking, eating, or dressing.
2. Duration — For the duration, omit internal narration and meet only sensation and movement.
3. Rejoin Activity — When commentary resumes, do not answer it; rejoin the activity at the next contact point.

rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Rejoin Activity”; notice the room.
• Pulled back? Touch “Duration”.
• “Duration” proves the present returned.
• What changed: “Choose Washing” → “Rejoin Activity”?
• I can use “Duration” to return here.

rituals.title: RUN THE TWO-WORD TASK
rituals.goal: Focus needs one live command, not the whole project shouting at once.
rituals.steps:
1. Scan Work — Look at the task and choose the single action verb needed for the next minute: read, compare, type, sort, call, or check.
2. Pick Verb — Choose the exact object receiving that action: paragraph, invoice, shelf, patient Name, pan, or message.
3. Bind Object — Join them into a two-word command such as TYPE SUMMARY or SORT RECEIPTS. Hide every other instruction for now.
4. Run Command — Run the command for sixty to ninety seconds. Stop only when the verb or object really needs to change.
rituals.win: ✓ The task stayed tiny enough to keep moving.
rituals.supports:
• One exhale after “Run Command”; redirect attention.
• Return once to “Bind Object”.
• “Bind Object” proves one signal leads.
• “Run Command”: what changed from “Scan Work”?
• I can use “Pick Verb” amid noise.

rituals.title: THE RELEVANCE BOUNCER
rituals.goal: Information must show a present purpose at the door.
rituals.steps:
1. Open Input — Before opening, reading, or following an input, ask whether it changes a current decision, action, or safety need.
2. Route It — If no, route it to later, reference, or delete.
3. Grant Attention — If yes, name the exact use before granting attention.

rituals.title: CLOSE THE ATTENTION TABS
rituals.goal: Interrupted tasks leave residue until a restart point exists.
rituals.steps:
1. Visit — Visit each abandoned item briefly.
2. Name Immediate Need — Hold the immediate resumption move and choose close, schedule, delegate, or resume.
3. Don't Perform — Do not do the tasks during the sweep.
4. End Active — End with one protected active tab and a written return address for the rest.
rituals.win: ✓ One tab stayed active; the others finally got a return address.
rituals.supports:

• Catch restart with “Don't Perform”.

• Compare “Visit” with “End Active”.
• I can use “Name Immediate Need” amid noise.

rituals.title: THE EMOTION STOPS AT THE SKIN
rituals.goal: Another person’s state is information, not automatic duty.
rituals.steps:
1. Emotion — Notice where their emotion seems to enter your body.
2. Trace Physical — Trace your physical boundary with gaze or touch.
3. State Action — State what action is yours, what remains theirs, and what you can offer without taking ownership.
4. Stay Blurred — Adjust distance if the distinction stays blurred.
rituals.win: ✓ Their emotion stopped at their skin; my duty stopped there too.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Stay Blurred”; release extra load.
• Skip replay; use “State Action”.
• “State Action” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• Look back: “Emotion” → “Stay Blurred”.
• I can use “Trace Physical” without carrying it all.
rituals.formula_flow: Emotion → Trace Physical → State Action → Stay Blurred
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Honour mandated or genuine care responsibilities rather than withdrawing reflexively.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: OPEN THE IDENTITY PORTFOLIO
rituals.goal: One role should not own every share of self.
rituals.steps:
1. Estimate Much — Name five identities active in your life and estimate how much attention each received this week.
2. Choose Neglected — Choose the neglected role that still matters.
3. Use Another Share — do one tiny action from its perspective today—friend, learner, neighbour, artist, caregiver, citizen.
rituals.win: ✓ I opened another share of myself and acted from it today.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Use Another Share”; mark the pause.
• Use “Choose Neglected” on return.
• “Choose Neglected” proves choice interrupted habit.
• At “Use Another Share”, compare “Estimate Much”.
• I can use “Choose Neglected” before autopilot.
rituals.formula_flow: Estimate Much → Choose Neglected → Use Another Share
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use role expansion to avoid urgent responsibilities in the dominant role.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: REMOVE THE AUDIENCE
rituals.goal: Find the choice that survives without witnesses.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine Nobody — Imagine nobody will see, praise, criticise, repost, or hear about the action.
2. Erase Audience — Erase the imagined audience one row at a time.
3. Choose Direct — What would you choose if only direct consequences and values remained?
4. Take Smallest — Take the smallest version privately.
rituals.win: ✓ Loss did not erase every direction.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Take Smallest”; keep the compass.
• If it flares, choose “Choose Direct”.
• “Choose Direct” keeps meaning in motion.
• Keep one lesson: “Imagine Nobody” → “Take Smallest”.
• I can use “Erase Audience” while pain stays real.
rituals.formula_flow: Imagine Nobody → Erase Audience → Choose Direct → Take Smallest
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep consultation where decisions emotion other people.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: MOVE THE MEMORY CAMERA
rituals.goal: You can preserve facts without re-entering the old viewpoint.
rituals.steps:
1. Place Memory — Place the memory on a screen with enough visual distance.
2. View Scene — View the scene from above, behind, or beside a compassionate observer.
3. Keep Events — Keep events accurate while changing camera position.
4. Add Resources — Add current-you outside the frame with present resources.
rituals.win: ✓ The memory camera moved, and the present kept its own frame.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Add Resources”; drop the scoreboard.
• Loop back? Use “Keep Events”.
• “Keep Events” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• What lost power: “Place Memory” → “Add Resources”?
• I can use “View Scene” without ranking my worth.
rituals.formula_flow: Place Memory → View Scene → Keep Events → Add Resources

rituals.title: ASK WHAT THE MEMORY IS STILL BILLING
rituals.goal: The memory can submit one claim without replaying the entire case.
rituals.steps:
1. Headline Event — State the event as one factual headline with no motive and no sensory replay.
2. Extract Claim — Finish this sentence once: ‘This memory still seems to demand ___.’ Keep only one claim.
3. Route Bill — Route the claim to BOUNDARY, REPAIR, GRIEF, or IMPOSSIBLE REVERSAL. Do not create a fifth category.
4. Act Present — Choose the matching present response: set protection, request safe repair, make room for grief, or stop billing today for a reversal history cannot provide.
rituals.win: ✓ The old bill met today’s receipt—and stopped charging the present.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Act Present”; end the lap.
• Skip replay; use “Route Bill”.
• “Route Bill” proves loops can stop.
• “Headline Event” → “Act Present”: what changed?
• I can use “Extract Claim” without another lap.
rituals.formula_flow: Headline Event → Extract Claim → Route Bill → Act Present
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not contact unsafe people, seek revenge, force reconciliation, or use this game during trauma flooding or immediate danger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE LAPSE FIRE DRILL
rituals.goal: One miss should trigger recovery, not identity collapse.
rituals.steps:
1. Name What Happened — Pre-plan three actions after a lapse: name what happened without judgement; restore the environment or schedule; do the next smallest valid repetition.
2. Store — Store the script beside the behaviour.
3. Use After — Use it after one miss—before a second is negotiated.
rituals.win: ✓ The comparison sting stayed local instead of becoming a life verdict.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Use After”; drop the scoreboard.
• On return, repeat “Store”.
• “Store” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• Keep one lesson: “Name What Happened” → “Use After”.
• I can use “Store” without ranking my worth.
rituals.formula_flow: Name What Happened → Store → Use After

rituals.title: UNDERSTAND, THEN DISAGREE CLEANLY
rituals.goal: Empathy does not sign their conclusion.
rituals.steps:
1. View They — Summarise their view until they could recognise it.
2. Name Need — Name the need or logic you understand.
3. Say Meaning — Then say exactly where your meaning, value, or decision differs.
4. Receive Own — No ‘but’ inside the summary; disagreement receives its own sentence.
rituals.win: ✓ I understood their view without signing their conclusion.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Receive Own”; let feeling settle.
• On return, repeat “Say Meaning”.
• “Say Meaning” separates feeling from fact.
• “View They” versus “Receive Own”: what eased?
• I can use “Name Need” while emotion stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: View They → Name Need → Say Meaning → Receive Own
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not require mutual understanding before protecting yourself.

rituals.title: ONE FIGHT, THREE TIME SCALES
rituals.goal: Today’s argument should not impersonate the whole relationship.
rituals.steps:
1. Issue Recurring — Check the immediate issue, the recurring pattern, and the full relationship history separately.
2. Give Own — Give each its own conclusion and action. Say what happened as if you were reporting it.
3. Don't Erase — Do not let a good history erase a harmful pattern or one incident erase all context.
rituals.win: ✓ One fight found its proper scale—without erasing the history or excusing the pattern.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Don't Erase”; soften the jaw.
• Skip replay; use “Give Own”.
• “Give Own” keeps clarity above heat.
• Difference check: “Issue Recurring” → “Don't Erase”.
• I can use “Give Own” without extra heat.
rituals.formula_flow: Issue Recurring → Give Own → Don't Erase
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.title: BURY THE GOAL, FREE THE ENERGY
rituals.goal: Some ambitions deserve a formal ending.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Goal — Name the goal, why it once mattered, what changed, and which obligations can now close.
2. Keep Value — Thank any value it revealed.
3. Bury the Goal — Cancel one concrete commitment, archive materials, and redirect the recovered resource toward a living priority.
rituals.win: ✓ I buried the dead goal and redirected the energy to something alive.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Bury the Goal”; watch the thought.
• Restart detected: “Keep Value”.
• “Keep Value” proves thought is observable.
• “Name Goal” versus “Bury the Goal”: what eased?
• I can use “Keep Value” without obeying thought.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Goal → Keep Value → Bury the Goal
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Distinguish wise closure from quitting during a temporary setback.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: POSSIBLE IS NOT PROBABLE
rituals.goal: Separate existence from likelihood and support.
rituals.steps:
1. State Lines — State three lines: It is possible that…; It is probable that…; The evidence currently supports….
2. Don't Allow — Do not allow content to migrate upward without justification.
3. Plan Probability — Base planning on chance and safety margin, not possibility alone.
rituals.win: ✓ Possible and probable finally stopped sharing a name tag.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Plan Probability”; leave the forecast.
• On return: “Don't Allow”.
• “Don't Allow” — fear isn’t fate.
• Look back: “State Lines” → “Plan Probability”.
• I can use “Don't Allow” while fear stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: State Lines → Don't Allow → Plan Probability

rituals.title: NOTICE THE SPACE DOING THE HOLDING
rituals.goal: Objects dominate because intervals are treated as nothing.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Forms — Choose three forms.
2. Attend Space — Attend to the space inside openings, around edges, and between objects.
3. Reverse Figure — Reverse figure and ground until space becomes as perceptible as matter.
4. Include Room — Include the room around your body.
rituals.win: ✓ Noticed the empty space doing part of the holding.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Include Room”; watch the thought.
• Loop back? Use “Reverse Figure”.
• “Reverse Figure” proves thought is observable.
• At “Include Room”, compare “Choose Forms”.
• I can use “Attend Space” without obeying thought.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Forms → Attend Space → Reverse Figure → Include Room
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Maintain object focus where navigation or task precision demands it.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: CHANGE THE SYMBOL’S JOB
rituals.goal: Unspoken experience may respond to transformation before explanation.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Image — Choose the image or object that represents the state.
2. Open Cage — Alter one property—open the cage, cool the metal, add roots, repair the crack, move the weight, give the storm a shoreline.
3. Observe Inner — Observe the inner response and translate it into one practical move.
rituals.win: ✓ The mind produced content; it did not produce a commander.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Observe Inner”; watch the thought.
• Restart detected: “Open Cage”.
• “Open Cage” proves thought is observable.
• Compare “Choose Image” with “Observe Inner”.
• I can use “Open Cage” without obeying thought.

2. Open Cage — Alter one property—open the cage, cool the metal, add roots, repair the crack, move the weight, give the storm a shoreline.
3. Observe Inner — Observe the inner response and translate it into one practical move.
display.win: ✓ The mind produced content; it did not produce a commander.
display.supports:
• Exhale after “Observe Inner”; watch the thought.
• Restart detected: “Open Cage”.
• “Open Cage” proves thought is observable.
• Compare “Choose Image” with “Observe Inner”.
• I can use “Open Cage” without obeying thought.
support_lines: Exhale after “Observe Inner”; watch the thought.
I can use “Open Cage” without obeying thought.
display.formula_flow: Choose Image → Open Cage → Observe Inner

PAUSE

rituals.title: CONSTRAINTS ENTER BEFORE OPTIONS
rituals.goal: Must-have limits should shape the field before desire fills it.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Safety — Picture safety, ethics, consent, resources, and timing constraints first.
2. Eliminate — Eliminate choices that violate them.
3. Generate — Generate options only inside the surviving space.
4. Lead With Constraints — Treat creativity as solving within reality, not arguing with the boundary.
rituals.win: ✓ I let the constraints shape the field before the options started campaigning.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Lead With Constraints”; release extra load.
• On return, repeat “Generate”.
• “Generate” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• At “Lead With Constraints”, compare “Picture Safety”.
• I can use “Eliminate” without carrying it all.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture Safety → Eliminate → Generate → Lead With Constraints
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Challenge assumed constraints that lack factual support.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
